articles.title: How Travis Kelce expanded beyond football with 13 investments, a $200M beer brand and ownership in his hometown team
articles.summary: Travis Kelce now has money in a beer company valued at about $200 million, a theme park giant, a mattress maker and his hometown baseball team.
articles.body: Travis Kelce now has money in a beer company valued at about $200 million, a theme park giant, a mattress maker and his hometown baseball team. The Chiefs tight end announced a minority stake in the Cleveland Guardians on May 27, adding to a list that already included Six Flags, Sleep Number and Alpine F1. Garage Beer, which he co-owns with his brother Jason, has been available at every U.S. Red Robin since July 21. None of it depends on his next catch. His 2026 Chiefs deal is reportedly a one-year contract.How did Travis Kelce expand beyond football with so many investments?The portfolio grew in layers. A CB Insights profile from early 2025 listed 12 investments and one exit, Cholula in 2020. The biggest deals have come fast since then. In October 2025, he joined activist firm Jana Partners and other investors in a group that holds about 9% of Six Flags, a stake The Wall Street Journal valued near $200 million. That figure covers the whole group, not Kelce alone. He calls himself a "lifelong Six Flags fan," and the timing was bold, since the company's shares fell more than 45% in 2025.Sleep Number followed in January. Kelce took a stake of under 5% and signed on for three years of national ads. He bought some shares himself and will receive restricted stock that vests over those three years. In March, Tommy Hilfiger named him a global brand ambassador in a multi-season deal. Fox 4 Kansas City also lists a stake in an Alpine Formula 1 team, an arena football team, a car wash company and the Kansas City steakhouse 1587 Prime.How much is Garage Beer worth, and does Travis Kelce own all of it?No. Garage Beer has several owners. Travis and Jason joined in June 2024 as co-owners and operators. In September 2025, private equity firm Durational Capital Management put money into the brand's first outside funding round, and The Wall Street Journal reported a valuation of roughly $200 million. CEO Andy Sauer said revenue was on track for $60 million to $70 million that year, up from under $20 million in 2024. Kelce's personal share has not been made public, so $200 million is the company's value, not his.The brand sells two beers, Classic Light and Lime. Both carry 4% alcohol and 95 calories. The Red Robin rollout makes the chain the first national restaurant group to serve Garage Beer in every U.S. location, which puts the product in front of diners and not only in coolers.Why did Travis Kelce buy into the Cleveland Guardians?Home, mostly. Kelce grew up in Cleveland Heights and played baseball at Cleveland Heights High School, where his father Ed coached him. The Guardians announced his minority purchase on May 27, and he called it a "dream come true for a Cleveland kid." The price and the size of his stake were not disclosed.One detail gives the deal extra weight. Partner David Blitzer can become the controlling owner after the 2027 season, or wait and use that option later. Kelce has bought into a group that could change leadership soon.Put the pieces side by side and the pattern is hard to miss. A beer brand, a theme park chain, a mattress company and a ballclub all pay off whether or not he keeps playing. He has never confirmed retirement plans. Two dates are already set: his Tommy Hilfiger project in New York this fall, and the Guardians' control decision after 2027.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ciara shows off $2M diamond as baby No. 5 is on the way, with fans convinced Russell Wilson has a tradition
articles.summary: Ciara is once again giving fans plenty to talk about, not just because of her growing baby bump, but also because of the eye-catching diamond ring she
articles.body: Ciara is once again giving fans plenty to talk about, not just because of her growing baby bump, but also because of the eye-catching diamond ring she recently showed off. The singer, who is expecting her fifth child and fourth with husband Russell Wilson, appeared in a stunning black lace maternity look while proudly displaying her pregnancy bump. But eagle-eyed fans quickly focused on the enormous ring on her finger.Ciara’s jaw-dropping ring sparks fan theory that Russell Wilson added a diamond for every babyOne fan reposted the footage and wrote, “My goodness what is that ring?? Russell put a new diamond on it for each new baby?? WOW.” The theory quickly caught attention online, with fans wondering whether Wilson has been adding diamonds to Ciara’s ring as their family has grown.The couple announced in September that they are expecting another child, with Ciara showing off her growing bump in a creative pregnancy reveal. Their announcement featured four shirts representing their existing children and a blank baby onesie for the newest addition. They captioned the post, “One more person to Love.”Ciara and Wilson are already parents to Sienna Princess, Win Harrison, and Amora Princess. Ciara also shares her eldest son, Future Zahir, with rapper Future. The upcoming arrival will be her fifth child and her fourth with Wilson. The pregnancy also fulfills Wilson’s long-running desire for another child. He had previously joked about wanting a fifth baby and even referred to the hoped-for addition as “Cinco.”But did Russell really add a diamond for every baby?That is where the viral fan theory gets interesting. There is no confirmed report or public statement from Ciara, Wilson or the jeweler establishing that Wilson adds a new diamond to her ring for every child. So while fans are speculating about the meaning behind the ring, the “one diamond for each baby” explanation should not be presented as a confirmed tradition.What is documented is that Wilson proposed to Ciara in 2016 with a spectacular diamond engagement ring, which has long been one of the standout pieces in her jewelry collection. Current celebrity-ring coverage continues to highlight the size and extravagance of the piece. That has not stopped fans from connecting the dots as Ciara prepares to become a mother of five. And with Ciara recently turning heads on the Paris Fashion Week runway while proudly showing off her baby bump, the singer is clearly embracing this pregnancy in typically glamorous fashion.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: How Patrick Mahomes uses 30+ Whataburger locations and 4 team stakes to build an off-field empire beyond his $450 million deal
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes signed a 10-year, $450 million extension with the Chiefs in 2020, and he has spent the years since turning part of that income into
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes signed a 10-year, $450 million extension with the Chiefs in 2020, and he has spent the years since turning part of that income into ownership. He holds stakes in four sports teams and sits inside KMO Burger, the group that operates 29 Whataburger restaurants across Kansas and Missouri and has aimed for 30 since day one. In June 2026, the Chiefs reworked his contract again, lifting it to $504.75 million through 2033, according to the Associated Press. The paycheck is the headline, but the stakes are where his long game sits.How does Patrick Mahomes build an off-field empire beyond his $450 million deal?Start with the paycheck, because it explains everything else. When Mahomes signed in July 2020, the headline number was $503 million. The base deal was $450 million over 10 years. The rest came from incentives and the last two years of his rookie contract. It was the richest contract in sports at the time, and it left one obvious question. What happens to a player whose income rides on a single left knee?Last December gave a blunt answer. Mahomes tore the ACL and LCL in that knee against the Chargers on Dec. 14, had surgery the next day and missed the last three games of a 6-11 season. He was back at practice by late May and was cleared without restrictions for the opener, according to reports. In June, the Chiefs reworked the deal again. The new version runs through 2033 at $504.75 million, with escalators that could lift it to $522.25 million, the AP reported. That averages $63.1 million a year.A salary depends on a healthy quarterback. A stake in a team or a restaurant group keeps working when he is on the sideline. That is the quiet logic behind every move below.How many Whataburger restaurants is Mahomes tied to?The story starts with ketchup. In 2018, Mahomes made his love for the brand public, and when Whataburger tweeted him a picture of its sauce and asked where to ship it, he wrote back, "I just want a store in Kansas City!"Three years later, it became a business. In August 2021, Whataburger announced KMO Burger, an investor-led franchise group that included Mahomes, with a plan for 30 restaurants from Wichita, Kansas, to St. Joseph, Missouri, over seven years. "I love Kansas City and I love Whataburger," Mahomes said at the time. The first KMO restaurant opened on June 7, 2022, on Parallel Parkway in Kansas City, Kansas, with a Mahomes jersey and a plaque for his No. 15 inside.The real jump came in May 2025. Whataburger put its 16 company-owned restaurants in the Kansas City and Springfield, Missouri, markets into a joint venture with KMO, which brought 13 of its own. KMO now operates all 29. "Our team at KMO Burger is ready to keep raising the bar," Mahomes said. Terms were not disclosed, so nobody outside the deal knows what his piece is worth. The chain itself had more than 1,100 restaurants in 16 states at that point, which makes this a regional franchise group, not a takeover of the brand.Which four teams does Mahomes own a piece of?The Royals came first. He bought into the Kansas City baseball club in July 2020, weeks after signing the extension, as a minority owner. A year later, on July 27, 2021, he joined the ownership group of Sporting Kansas City. ESPN reported that he had already attended at least 12 matches by then and had even led fans in a chant at Children's Mercy Park.The next two came close together. In December 2022, he joined the group behind the Miami Pickleball Club in Major League Pickleball, alongside Naomi Osaka, Nick Kyrgios and agent Rich Paul. Forbes reported that expansion fees for comparable teams ran from $1 million to $3 million. Then, on Jan. 10, 2023, he joined his wife, Brittany, as an owner of the Kansas City Current in the NWSL. The club said he was the first active NFL player with equity in a team in that league.Put together, the list reads like a map of his interests: baseball, soccer, women's sports and a fast-growing paddle game.Why does Mahomes keep investing in Kansas City first?Three of the four teams sit in one metro area, and so do most of the burger restaurants. That is not an accident. In a mid-sized market, a face that fans trust can move a team's brand more than the same face would in New York or Los Angeles. The quarterback gets equity that grows with the city, and the city gets a hometown name behind its clubs.The Whataburger deal is the most telling piece, mostly because it is the least glamorous. A drive-thru that stays open around the clock is a daily, repeatable business. KMO also backs charities such as Make-A-Wish and Special Olympics through Mahomes' foundation, Franchise Times reported, so the restaurants carry some community weight too.None of it is risk-free. Minority stakes give little say over decisions, restaurant margins run thin, and a young pickleball league has not yet proved it will last. What keeps the mix sensible is scale. A $1 million to $3 million team buy-in is a small slice next to a $450 million deal.Can Mahomes own an NFL team one day?He says that is the goal. In 2023, when he joined an ownership group in Formula 1, Mahomes talked about owning an NFL team once he retires and noted that Tom Brady was already working on it. "That's definitely where you want to get to," he said, as ESPN relayed.The Chiefs now hold his contract through 2033, when he will be 38. Between now and then, the Whataburger group, the four teams and the Formula 1 stake read like a long application for a seat in the owners' box.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "It was weird": Mike Vrabel and Dianna Russini controversy gets fresh twist from ex-Raiders star
articles.summary: Former Las Vegas Raiders star Richie Incognito has brought a 2019 memory back into the spotlight amid renewed interest in the controversy surrounding Mike
articles.body: Former Las Vegas Raiders star Richie Incognito has brought a 2019 memory back into the spotlight amid renewed interest in the controversy surrounding Mike Vrabel and Dianna Russini. Incognito recalled meeting Vrabel at a Super Bowl party in Miami and said the then-Tennessee Titans coach introduced him to Russini during their conversation. The retired NFL offensive lineman admitted that the introduction struck him as unusual at the time, adding another detail to a story that has attracted major attention around the NFL.Richie Incognito recalls Mike Vrabel and Dianna Russini meetingIncognito shared the story during Saturday's episode of the Initial Contact show. He was discussing a Super Bowl party hosted by NFL insider Jay Glazer after the 2019 season when he remembered running into Vrabel.The former Raiders lineman said the two first spoke about their teams' meeting that season. Oakland had faced Tennessee, and Incognito recalled Vrabel praising the Raiders' offensive line.He then described how the conversation shifted when Vrabel introduced him to Russini."I got a good Vrabel-Russini story," Incognito said. "It's after the 2019 season. We're down in Miami and it's a Super Bowl party. Jay Glazer throws this great Super Bowl party at like this auto collection place. There's all these exotic cars, and the Oakland Raiders have played the Tennessee Titans that year.""So I see Vrabel at the party, and I go up, and I'm like, 'Hey Vrabes, you guys were tough. We should have won that game.' He's like, 'Listen, you guys were some dudes. That's the biggest offensive line we've ever faced. I told my guys they had to be ready. You guys brought it.' So me and Vrabel are having this conversation, and mid-conversation, he goes, 'Oh, let me introduce you to Dianna Russini.' And I go, 'Oh, hey, what's up, Dianna? How you doing?' And I always thought it was weird."Incognito's account is a recollection of an encounter from several years ago. His comment about finding the introduction unusual reflects his own reaction at the time and does not, by itself, establish anything beyond the meeting he described.Mike Vrabel and Dianna Russini controversy returns to NFL spotlightThe story has resurfaced after photos involving Vrabel and Russini from previous years triggered widespread online speculation during the offseason. The controversy eventually became a major talking point across NFL media.Russini later resigned from her position at The Athletic. Vrabel, meanwhile, remains focused on his coaching career and is in his second season with the New England Patriots.The Patriots entered Sunday's matchup against the Buffalo Bills with a 1-2 record after three games. While the on-field season has moved forward, Incognito's story has renewed interest in an episode that dates back to the 2019 NFL season.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Russell Wilson and Ciara donate $250,000 as Spokane families face the aftermath of historic wildfires
articles.summary: Russell Wilson and Ciara are stepping in to help Spokane families facing the long road back after a devastating wildfire season.
articles.body: Russell Wilson and Ciara are stepping in to help Spokane families facing the long road back after a devastating wildfire season. Their Why Not You Foundation has committed $250,000 to The Salvation Army of Spokane, with the money aimed at both urgent relief and longer-term support. The donation comes as communities continue dealing with destroyed homes, evacuations, financial pressure and disrupted services. Rather than limiting the gift to emergency response, the foundation’s contribution will also help families access food, child care, education and other essential programmes in the months ahead.Russell Wilson and Ciara donate $250,000 to Spokane familiesThe $250,000 donation arrives as Spokane County and other parts of Eastern Washington work through the damage left by the 2026 wildfires. The Salvation Army will use the funding to respond to families affected by the fires while continuing services for people facing hardship throughout the year.Captain David Cain, director of The Salvation Army of Spokane, said the contribution gives the organisation room to respond to changing needs.“This gift allows us to respond to families who have been impacted by the wildfires while also ensuring that families who are struggling can access support throughout the year,” Cain said.The money will support several programmes, including the Hope Market Food Bank and Family Resource Center, After the Bell after-school services, and back-to-school, summer camp and Christmas assistance.It will also help Sally’s House and Evangeline’s House, which provide emergency foster care for children arriving from unsafe or abusive homes.That wider reach matters because recovery does not end when evacuation orders are lifted. Families can face new costs long after a fire has passed, from replacing essentials to finding stable care and getting children back into normal routines.Spokane wildfire recovery gets support from Russell Wilson and CiaraThe scale of the disaster underlines why donations such as the Wilsons’ are important. A preliminary assessment found that the fires destroyed 649 primary residences, damaged another 2,542 homes and burned nearly 369,000 acres across affected areas.Spokane County suffered some of the heaviest losses. More than 65,000 people were evacuated, while hundreds of homes were destroyed or damaged. Essential services, healthcare and utilities were also disrupted.Cain stressed that the foundation's investment can reach families dealing with very different challenges.“Whether a family has lost something because of a wildfire, is struggling to put food on the table, is worried about sending their children back to school, or simply needs a little help getting through the holidays, this investment will make a tangible difference” Cain said.The donation therefore extends beyond immediate wildfire relief. It gives The Salvation Army additional resources to keep helping families as Spokane moves from emergency response toward rebuilding and recovery.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: $30 billion sports giant could turn Travis Kelce’s post-NFL chapter into a major media career
articles.summary: Travis Kelce may have another major stage waiting for him whenever his NFL career finally comes to an end.
articles.body: Travis Kelce may have another major stage waiting for him whenever his NFL career finally comes to an end. The Kansas City Chiefs star has already shown that his appeal extends well beyond the football field, and ESPN could be among the networks interested in that star power. For now, though, Kelce is firmly focused on playing. His strong start to the 2026 season has only added to the uncertainty over when he might walk away.Travis Kelce's ESPN opportunity could grow after retirementKelce's television future is attracting attention because he has already proved he can handle a microphone. His connection with ESPN also has an interesting link through Joe Buck, who continues to call Monday Night Football with Troy Aikman.Buck signed a six-year extension with ESPN in September 2026. The network is also preparing to broadcast Super Bowl LXI in February 2027. That gives ESPN a strong platform for former players who can bring both football knowledge and personality to its coverage.Still, there is no deal between Kelce and ESPN. Any suggestion that he is joining the network remains speculation until the Chiefs star announces his retirement and chooses his next career move.Travis Kelce's media experience gives him an edgeKelce would not enter broadcasting as a complete newcomer. He hosted Saturday Night Live in 2023 and later became the host of Prime Video's Are You Smarter Than a Celebrity? He also co-hosts New Heights with his brother Jason Kelce, giving him years of experience speaking freely about football, sports culture and entertainment.Jason's own move into broadcasting could make the transition even more natural. After retiring from the Philadelphia Eagles, he joined ESPN as an analyst on Monday Night Countdown in 2024. Travis has watched that path unfold while building his own media profile.His playing career also gives him plenty to discuss. Kelce entered the 2026 season with three Super Bowl titles, seven All-Pro selections and more than 13,000 receiving yards. More importantly, his recent form suggests retirement may still be some distance away.Through three games this season, Kelce had 14 catches for 231 yards and two touchdowns. He led the Chiefs in all three receiving categories while helping Kansas City open the campaign 3-0.So, while ESPN could eventually be an appealing destination, Kelce has little reason to rush into the next chapter. For now, the Chiefs tight end still looks like he has plenty left to give on the field.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Travis Kelce’s $200 million Six Flags investment takes an unexpected turn in 22 year old college graduate’s death lawsuit
articles.summary: Travis Kelce, the Kansas City Chiefs’ star tight end, has kept his focus on winning a Super Bowl for his team this season amid criticism about his fitness
articles.body: Travis Kelce, the Kansas City Chiefs’ star tight end, has kept his focus on winning a Super Bowl for his team this season amid criticism about his fitness levels. While he has been a strong player on the field, his $200 million investment had fallen into controversial legal trouble. Amid the new season, it seems things have taken a turn again.Travis Kelce’s $200 million investment in Six Flags has a new twist after being involved in a wrongful death lawsuitAccording to FOX 11 Los Angeles, Travis Kelce’s Six Flags has now reached a settlement agreement with ride-train supplier S&S Worldwide Inc., after the amusement park was sued by Christopher Howley’s family for his tragic death in 2022.For now, the financial details have been kept private as his family has tried to remain out of the spotlight.In June 2022, 22 year old college graduate Chritopher Howley collapsed after going on the infamous X2 ride with his younger brother, Alex, and cousins.As per reports, a CT scan revealed a catastrophic subdural hematoma, and the Los Angeles County Department of Medical Examiner ended up ruling his death an accident resulting from blunt force head trauma sustained on the ride.The young man Christopher Howley passed away in just a few hours leaving behind his family shaken and grieving.As per FOX 11, in an interview, Christopher Howley’s mother said, "I remember him [Alex] saying, 'Mom, Christopher collapsed, and he's not waking up…We went from a family of four to a family of three in an instant…”She added, “It's devastating. It is a piece of us that is gone forever."His younger brother, Alex, also opened up about the ride as he said, "It was very rough. It just jerked us. It just jerked us all around," and noting that near the end, "It just like jolted us all the way forward and then our heads just swung all the way back into the end to the head."Christopher Howley’s father William added, "The surgeon had said, he likened it to shaken baby syndrome, that the ride hit his heard so hard that it had basically ruptured his brain…”In the last few months, many such people have complained of getting sick after being on the ride. Two women were even hospitalised and had to go through brain surgery after getting on the X2 in July 2026.The infamous X2 ride has now been shut down permanently as Six Flags continues to fight several lawsuits related to the ride.Travis Kelce keeps his distance from Six Flags’ legal troubleThough Travis Kelce invested a whopping $200 million into Six Flags for a 9% stake alongside JANA Partners, he has kept himself away from the mess.There have been no statements or comments from the star player yet.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes, the Kansas City Chiefs’ popular quarterback, has his eyes on the Super Bowl this time after his brutal injuries ended the season early
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes, the Kansas City Chiefs’ popular quarterback, has his eyes on the Super Bowl this time after his brutal injuries ended the season early for the team in the last season. The Kansas City Chiefs have remained unbeatable as the team currently enjoys a winning streak. Amid this, one of Patrick Mahomes’ investments seems to be planning for the future.Patrick Mahomes investment in WHOOP works out as the health tech brand plans new launchesThe Kansas City Chiefs’ popular quarterback Patrick Mahomes was one of the initial investors in the health tech brand WHOOP in 2020.In a recent interview with Gulf Business, WHOOP founder and CEO Will Ahmed opened up about the new plans as he said, “WHOOP 5.0 and WHOOP MG introduce medical-grade capabilities and insights never before offered in a single wearable. The new sensors deliver 14 days of battery life — three times what our last device offered — while being 7 per cent smaller. WHOOP MG builds on that with Heart Screener with ECG, Irregular Heart Rhythm Notifications, and Blood Pressure Insights.”WHOOP founder and CEO Will Ahmed added, “We’ve also introduced new software features including Healthspan with WHOOP Age, updated Sleep Performance, Hormonal Insights, and an improved Steps experience — all designed to help members perform better and live longer.This isn’t just a product update. It’s the biggest leap forward in WHOOP technology to date, not just to our hardware, but to the entire WHOOP experience.”While Patrick Mahomes has not responded to this, he has always remained loyal to WHOOP.The star quarterback invested in WHOOP in October 2020 during its $100 million Series E funding round, which valued the wearable fitness technology startup at $1.2 billion.Before he invested into the health tech brand, Patrick Mahomes was public about how he has already integrated the screenless biometric tracker into his NFL recovery regimen to optimize his sleep and heart rate data.While the star quarterback invested into the brand, his deal with WHOOP also made him a brand ambassador of the brand.In the last few months, Patrick Mahomes’ investment in WHOOP turned highly profitable as the company’s valuation skyrocketed to $10.1 billion following a massive $575 million Series G funding round, co-investors like LeBron James and Cristiano Ronaldo joining in on the round.Patrick Mahomes turns strategic about his investments as he stays focused on his careerOver the last few years, as Patrick Mahomes remained a strong player on the field, he has also been pretty strategic about his investments.The three time Super Bowl Most Valuable Player has been consistently investing in emerging brands and has been able to expand his investment portfolio.Amid the Week 4’s win against the Las Vegas Raiders, all eyes remain on Patrick Mahomes.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 5 momentous plays: Nick Sirianni's field-goal decision, plus Kamari Lassiter's painful penalties
articles.summary: Here are some of the bigger but less-than-obvious momentum shifters in Sunday's games.
articles.body:
Week 4 wasn't quite the closely contested affair that Week 3 was , but there still were several one-score games that were decided by a handful of key plays.

A few were bad luck. Some of the close games came down to a handful of plays. But there were some below-the-radar moments in several of the tight ones that shifted the tides.

Here are some of the bigger but less-than-obvious momentum shifters in Sunday's games:

1. Kamari Lassiter's nightmare drive haunts Texans

Midway through the third quarter, the Texans led the Cowboys 23-13, and had Dallas in a third-and-7 at the Houston 8-yard line. It appeared Houston got a stop, but Texans cornerback Kamari Lassiter — who allowed a 53-yard catch earlier on the drive — was flagged for a back-breaking pass interference call.

Houston held firm the next three plays, moving the Cowboys back two yards. But on fourth-and-goal from the 3-yard line, Lassiter again was flagged, this time for holding. Houston couldn't hold again, as Javonte Williams' TD cut the Texans' lead to three.

That series completely flipped the game, one Dallas stormed back to win in the final minute .

The Texans were actually on the right side of a few big momentum plays before and after this. They blocked a field-goal try near the end of the first half, kicking their own FG for a six-point swing in a 30-second span. They also converted a third-and-14 hook-and-ladder play for 21 yards, setting up Houston's go-ahead TD with 2:26 remaining in the game.

But not getting that goal-line stop potentially cost them four points … in a four-point loss.

Lassiter is a talented, young player, but he and the Texans are in a dark place right now at 0-4.

The most controversial momentum swing came when Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni opted to go for it on fourth-and-goal from the 2, instead of kicking a field goal, leading 20-10 with 7:26 remaining against the visiting Rams. Jalen Hurts' pass was incomplete, and the Eagles got zero points out of the drive.

Perhaps trying to go for the kill shot there wasn't the worst idea in an effort to make it a three-possession game. A field goal would have given the Eagles a 13-point lead, but the Rams scored two TDs after that stop, so that one play didn't tilt the game by itself.

But Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley — filling in for an injured Saquon Barkley — had been running effectively on the drive, grinding away at the Rams. Hurts also is one of the better short-yardage running QBs in the game, although the Rams had stuffed a tush push late in the third quarter, which surely had to factor into Sirianni's thinking. It also didn't help that Hurts' timing on the third-and-goal play was thrown off by Cam Jurgens pulling too quickly, resulting in a no-gain.

Whether or not Sirianni made the right call, it backfired. Matthew Stafford looked down and out after his previous five possessions came up empty, but this was the spark he and his offense needed.

The Rams drove 98 yards on their ensuing drive to keep the game alive, and after the Eagles' 64-second three-and-out, the Rams went down and scored again for the improbable win .

The Eagles are in rough injury shape, and they've now lost two straight. Monday's loss in Chicago was a laugher, but they had Sunday's game in good shape before the late collapse.

3. Key INT, review help Packers hold off Bucs

In the final minute of the first half, the Bucs and Packers were tied at 7-all. Six game minutes later, the Bucs were down 10. Losing the middle portion of the game cost them dearly.

Rookie QB Jalon Daniels, filling in for an injured Baker Mayfield, threw a first-quarter interception, yet he was holding his own. Then Daniels threw his second pick of the first half, with Packers linebacker Edgerrin Cooper diving to make the grab and running it back 18 yards into Bucs territory.

That set up a Trey Smack 58-yard field goal and a little bump for the Packers before halftime. On their first possession of the second half, Jordan Love hit Tucker Kraft for a touchdown. Initially, it was called incomplete but later overturned after replay — and it was hardly obvious whether Kraft's foot clearly hit before he secured the catch.

It was an ugly game. Cooper left with an Achilles injury. Kaleb Johnson fumbled inside the 5-yard line. Love had a chance to make it a 10-point lead with four minutes left, but he threw an interception. The Packers were 2 for 10 on third downs.

The Bucs made their share of mistakes, too. But misplaying the middle section of the game, rookie quarterback or not, put them in an even tougher spot to pull off the upset .

The Raiders couldn't keep their unbeaten streak going, falling to the Chiefs , but they made Kansas City earn that victory in Las Vegas. Had a few more plays gone the Raiders' way, who knows?

Dareke Young's fumble on a kickoff, trailing 23-19 with 3:21 left in the game, was the obvious late momentum shift — and, yes, it hurt badly, even if the Raiders had a chance to tie or take the lead on their final drive.

But there was an earlier shift that cost the Raiders three points that head coach Klint Kubiak might now be regretting.

Three minutes into the second half, the Raiders' Matt Gay hit a 41-yard field goal to temporarily put the Raiders up 16-10. But the Chiefs were flagged for illegal formation on the kick, and Kubiak opted to take the points off the board — in spite of it not giving them an automatic first down.

Kirk Cousins' fourth-and-2 pass to Ashton Jeanty fell incomplete. The score remained 13-10, and the Raiders ended up losing by three points.

Kubiak might also regret predicting the Raiders would win during his halftime interview. Not too long later, his field-goal decision hurt his team.

5. Bell's nullified touchdown sunk Dolphins

There has been talk about the possibility of the Dolphins going winless this season, but with a few more breaks, they might have been able to take down the Vikings in Minnesota.

The biggest play that went against them was a tremendous touchdown that evaporated into thin air almost as fast as it happened.

Early in the second quarter, Malik Willis scrambled and — off-balance and falling out of bounds — threw what appeared to be a 68-yard TD to talented rookie wide receiver Chris Bell on a third-and-4 play. For the briefest of moments, Miami was leading 3-0, and the U.S. Bank Stadium crowd was stunned.

But Bell was flagged for illegal touching, having stepped out of bounds on his own prior to the catch, which wiped out what would have been his first career touchdown. The penalty came with a loss of downs, forcing a punt. The Vikings went down and kicked the second of their five field goals on the day in a 15-10 win.

Miami finished the first half with only 76 yards on 21 plays. The Dolphins' offense got going a bit with a 10-point third quarter, but that's all the group could muster. The Bell touchdown would have changed the game dramatically.

The Dolphins scored the only touchdown in the game — and they should have had two — but the Vikings held on for victory. That's how much separated the winless Dolphins and the unbeaten Vikings playing in their home stadium.

articles.title: “Every bone in his body cracked”: Chop Robinson escapes NFL fine after controversial Patrick Mahomes hit as the Kansas City Chiefs star reveals his condition
articles.summary: Chop Robinson came away from a controversial hit on Patrick Mahomes without an NFL fine.
articles.body: Chop Robinson came away from a controversial hit on Patrick Mahomes without an NFL fine. The Dolphins pass rusher drew a roughing-the-passer flag during Miami’s Week 3 game against the Kansas City Chiefs on Oct. 4, 2026. The call gave Kansas City a fresh set of downs, but Robinson avoided further punishment when the league released its Week 3 accountability report.The play came late in the third quarter with the Chiefs backed up at their own 5-yard line. Mahomes dropped back on third-and-9, and Robinson closed in from the edge just after the quarterback released a pass toward Rashee Rice. The pass fell incomplete, but Robinson drove Mahomes into the turf and drew the flag.Chop Robinson avoids NFL punishment after Patrick Mahomes collisionThe NFL released its Week 3 accountability report after the game, listing 30 plays that led to fines. Robinson did not appear among them. That kept the roughing call at an in-game penalty rather than turning it into an additional financial punishment.Robinson also accepted the call after the play, even though he admitted he did not know what else he could have done. Speaking after the game, the Dolphins pass rusher said, “I’m honestly not too sure, but either way, that’s what they called, so that’s what we got to play on. Next play.” He later added that he could have put his hands out earlier while falling.The penalty proved costly for Miami. The Chiefs would have faced a third-down stop deep in their own territory, but the penalty kept the drive alive. Kansas City then marched 80 yards on 13 plays, with Harrison Butker hitting a field goal that pushed the score to 17-10 in the fourth quarter. Patrick Mahomes walks away from Chop Robinson’s hit without missing timeThe collision looked concerning because Mahomes briefly grabbed his back after getting up. Still, the Chiefs quarterback stayed in the game and continued running the offense. Kansas City went on to beat Miami 24-10 and improved to 3-0.Chiefs head coach Andy Reid later joked about the force of the hit while discussing the quarterback’s ability to get back up. Speaking after the game, Reid said, “every bone in his body cracked,” before noting that Mahomes continued playing.Patrick Mahomes also brushed off the collision after the game. After the game, the QB said, “I’m doing great. It was like a natural chiropractor, so I felt better after the game, so I’m doing fine.”He finished with 246 passing yards, two touchdowns and one interception, and he did not miss a snap after Robinson’s hit.For Robinson, the NFL’s decision closes the issue without a fine. For Mahomes, the bigger takeaway was simple: the hit hurt, but it did not stop him from finishing the game.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce’s $6 million Pennsylvania compound faces issues with neighbors as many complained against them
articles.summary: Jason Kelce, the former Philadelphia Eagles' star player, has always been pretty protective of privacy concerning his wife, Kylie Kelce and their four
articles.body: Jason Kelce, the former Philadelphia Eagles' star player, has always been pretty protective of privacy concerning his wife, Kylie Kelce and their four daughters. While both Jason Kelce and his wife, popular podcaster Kylie Kelce prefer to keep their children out of the spotlight, the former NFL player had fought with his neighbors concerning his $6 million Pennsylvania compound.Jason Kelce’s tiff with neighbors over wanting to secure his and Kylie Kelce’s 10 acre compound in PennsylvaniaA few months ago, Jason Kelce went before the local zoning board to get legal permission in Haverford Township to drastically reshape his 10 acre estate.The former Philadelphia Eagles’ star player was trying to build a new custom luxury mansion as the primary family home for his growing family. To make room for it, he planned to demolish the older structures on the adjacent plots he had previously purchased.The land leveling is what triggered the battle with his neighbors. Many of Jason Kelce’s neighbors argued that flattening the natural hillsides would ruin the area's drainage, forcing massive amounts of stormwater runoff directly into their own luxury yards.At the end, as Jason Kelce spoke about wanting more security for his family, his plea was accepted by the local zoning board in Haverford Township.In an interview with WGAL, Travis Kelce opened up about it as he said, "We want to be in this area, we like this area a lot…Obviously, things for my family are quite unique with the security purposes. We'd like to just deter a little bit of the foot traffic coming in and out of the home."The popular entrepreneur and ESPN sports analyst added, "We were trying to put a fence that sufficiently [deters foot traffic], but also appeals to the aesthetic of the area and that people would appreciate," he said.Jason Kelce and his wife, Kylie Kelce, built a 10 acre compound in Pennsylvania ever since they got marriedFor the unversed, Jason Kelce and his wife, Kylie Kelce, bought out neighboring properties in the upscale Philadelphia suburb of Haverford Township, Pennsylvania, to construct a secure family compound ever since they bought their first home there in 2018.In 2018, Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce bought a 4-bedroom, 2.5-bathroom property on Coopertown Road for $680,000. Just two years later, in 2020, they purchased an adjoining 8 acre parcel of land for $3.96 million.In 2023, Jason Kelce and his wife, Kylie Kelce, added a third adjacent property for $1.35 million, bringing the total estate size to roughly 10 acres and their total land investment to $6 million.For now, Jason Kelce and his wife, Kylie Kelce, have found their home here with their four daughters.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: “I felt like an idiot”: Travis Kelce ended up with a $24,309 NFL fine after throwing a towel at an official and joking about 1,715 Nicolas Cage pillow cases
articles.summary: Travis Kelce’s frustration with an NFL official cost him $24,309 in 2016. On Nov.
articles.body: Travis Kelce’s frustration with an NFL official cost him $24,309 in 2016. On Nov. 6, the Kansas City Chiefs tight end threw his towel toward an official during a 19-14 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars. The unusual move earned him a second unsportsmanlike conduct penalty and an ejection.The NFL announced Kelce’s fine on Nov. 11, 2016. Yet the Chiefs star did not let the hefty punishment end there. Instead, he turned the fine into a joke, asking fans on Twitter what he could buy with $24,309. His answer included 1,715 Nicolas Cage pillow cases.How a missed pass interference call started the incidentThe whole trouble began in the fourth quarter of the Nov. 6 game. Kelce believed Jaguars cornerback Prince Amukamara committed pass interference in the end zone, but officials did not throw a flag.Travis Kelce argued with two officials over the no-call. He received his first unsportsmanlike conduct penalty during the exchange. That still did not end his frustration.Kelce then pulled the towel from the waistband of his uniform and threw it toward an official. The gesture mocked the way officials throw penalty flags during games.Field Judge Mike Weatherford responded by throwing his cap toward Kelce. Another official then gave Kelce his second unsportsmanlike conduct penalty, which resulted in his ejection.The Chiefs still won the game 19-14, but Kelce’s exit became one of the biggest talking points afterward.Kelce acknowledged that he had gone too far. Speaking after the Chiefs’ victory on November 6, he said, “I felt like an idiot. I can’t do that to my teammates. It was a terrible decision.”He also joked about the unusual exchange with the officials, saying, “I can’t throw my flag on the ref, but he can throw his all day long.” Travis Kelce turned the $24,309 fine into a jokeFive days after the game, the NFL handed Kelce a $24,309 fine for his conduct toward the official. The amount quickly became part of the story because Kelce found an unusual way to deal with it. After the league announced the fine, Travis Kelce went to Twitter and asked fans what he could purchase with $24,309. Among his calculations was a bizarre option: 1,715 Nicolas Cage pillow cases.The joke gave the incident a lighter ending, but Travis Kelce already had a history of NFL fines. In 2014, the league fined him $11,205 after he made an unsportsmanlike gesture near a referee who announced a penalty.The 2016 incident, however, had a different twist. A missed call sparked Kelce’s argument, the argument led to a towel toss, the towel toss ended his game and the ejection eventually came with a $24,309 bill. articles.title: NFL reportedly 'looking into' official sharing words with Cardinals' Trey McBride after dispute over no-call
articles.summary: There were no microphones nearby, so what Seeman said is left strictly up to the interpretation of lip readers. But Seeman clearly wasn't telling McBride to...
articles.body:
NFL line judge Jeff Seeman had some choice words for Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride on Sunday and the league is reportedly looking into the incident.

CBS cameras caught those words, much to the delight of McBride who laughed and pointed it out as soon as he realized that a camera was pointed at the official during the Cardinals' game at the New York Giants.

There were no microphones nearby, so what Seeman said is left strictly up to the interpretation of lip readers. But Seeman clearly wasn't telling McBride to have a nice day.

The interaction caught the attention of NFL Players Association executive director JC Tretter, who called on the NFL to hold Seeman accountable while sharing video on social media of the incident.

"This kind of behavior from an official towards a player is unacceptable," Tretter wrote. "Players are consistently held accountable when the roles are reversed. We expect the NFL to hold officials to the same standard."

Shortly after Tretter's tweet, The Athletic's Jonathan Jones reported that the NFL stated that it's "looking into the matter."

The interaction took place after game officials declined to call pass interference on a critical failed third-down pass from Jacoby Brissett to McBride. Giants cornerback Dru Phillips had coverage on the play and made contact with McBride before the ball arrived. McBride immediately protested the no-call to Seeman, who was standing next to the play. McBride's protests were to no avail and eventually drew the response seen above.

The Cardinals trailed 27-24 at the time of the incompletion and punted on the next play with 4:53 remaining in regulation. The Giants won the game 36-24.

McBride didn't address Seeman's comments with reporters postgame. The subject did not come up in the postgame pool report.

articles.title: Chiefs reportedly having discussions with Tyreek Hill about potential reunion after latest injuries
articles.summary: The stars are starting to align with a Chiefs-Tyreek Hill reunion after Sunday. The two sides have been in communication and with recent injuries the possibi...
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs had a very important divisional game on Sunday as they went against the Las Vegas Raiders , who were also undefeated. In what was a very tight game, the Chiefs were able to escape with a road win.

Kansas City did suffer some major injuries to its WR room, with the first being Rashee Rice. Then, Tyquan Thornton suffered a dislocated ankle in the fourth quarter.

"Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Tyquan Thornton suffered a dislocated left ankle Sunday that was later put back into place by team doctors, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. Thornton exited Allegiant Stadium on crutches after his team's 30-27 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. In the fourth quarter, he had to be carted off the field after he made a 55-yard catch that ended when he was tackled from behind by rookie free safety Treydan Stukes," ESPN's Nate Taylor wrote.

Despite the win, it came with a cost. The possibility of the Chiefs signing a WR is pretty high now. Taylor reported that the organization has been in contact with Tyreek Hill.

"Even before the injuries to Thornton and fellow receiver Rashee Rice on Sunday, the Chiefs had already shown interest in signing wide receiver Tyreek Hill, who is a free agent. Following Sunday's game, a team source said "we've remained in contact" with Hill and his agent Drew Rosenhaus," Taylor wrote.

This would be something, but the position is a necessity. At the beginning of September, Hill's agent Drew Rosenhaus gave a timeframe.

"Free-agent wide receiver Tyreek Hill and his representatives are "playing it on the safe side" as he prepares for a possible return to the NFL this season. His agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said Wednesday on The Pat McAfee Show that teams have shown interest in the eight-time Pro Bowler. However, doctors have advised Hill to delay a comeback until at least October," Bleacher Report's Joseph Zucker wrote.

It has been over a year since Hill's devastating injury to his leg, and it has been five years since his last game with Kansas City. This reunion would be one that the Chiefs need to make happen with their injuries.

Both sides will likely continue to discuss some things, but if Rice doesn't get a good report, it might be Hill's time to return to Kansas City. No one had this on their bingo card, and it very well could happen after the latest report.

articles.title: ‘This state belongs to Dallas’ – Fans erupt as Cowboys rally past Texans 34-30
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys fans erupted after their team came from behind to beat the Houston Texans 34-30 in a thrilling Texas showdown at NRG Stadium. The Cowboys trai...
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys fans erupted after their team came from behind to beat the Houston Texans 34-30 in a thrilling Texas showdown at NRG Stadium.

The Cowboys trailed 16-6 at half-time before turning the game around after the break. Dak Prescott eventually found CeeDee Lamb for the winning 12-yard touchdown with 40 seconds left.

Lamb was the star of the comeback, finishing with 17 catches for 189 yards and a touchdown. Javonte Williams also scored three rushing touchdowns as Dallas improved to 2-2.

Cowboys fans celebrate CeeDee Lamb after comeback win

Unsurprisingly, Lamb received plenty of praise from Cowboys supporters after his huge performance.

One fan simply posted: "WHAT A DAY FOR CEEDEE LAMB"

Another celebrated the comeback while already looking ahead to the reaction from Dallas supporters, writing: "down 10 at half and still won in Houston. Cowboys fans are gonna be unbearable this week"

Lamb's performance also prompted a bold declaration from another supporter: "CeeDee Lamb is the best wide receiver in the NFL"

The comeback meant plenty to Cowboys fans, with one writing: "I was fervently praying for you today!! Way to go Cowboys"

Another supporter highlighted the dramatic turnaround after half-time: "Cowboys really came alive in the 2nd half"

Houston had been unable to contain Lamb when it mattered most, prompting one fan to joke: "Texans couldn't 'silence the Lamb.'"

The win also sparked some classic Texas bragging rights, with one supporter declaring: "This state belongs to the Dallas Cowboys!!!"

Another took things even further, writing: "There's only one true king of Texas and the NFL… and that's my beloved Cowboys #DALvsHOU"

Dallas now sits at 2-2 after recovering from a difficult first half and will take plenty of confidence from the way Prescott and Lamb delivered when the game was on the line. For Houston, the loss leaves the Texans still searching for their first win after letting another late lead slip away.
